page: Microsoft Azure E8s_v3 is an ESv3-family virtual machine configured with 8 vCPUs and 64.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, this instance features 4 physical cores with Hyper-Threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 50 MB L3 cache, 32 KB L1d cache, and 0.25 MB L2 cache. The hardware configuration includes a 131 GB local storage drive and supports Premium Storage, though it does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations position the E8s_v3 in the average tier for memory operations and specific database tasks, while raw CPU performance falls into the lower quartile. The instance achieved average ratings in Passmark CPU tests (7620.18) and Passmark memory tests (2294.36). Memory bandwidth is measured at 365.1 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and approximately 42.29 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core and multi-core stress-ng tests, along with Geekbench single-core (1017.0) and multi-core (3995.0) scores, are categorized in the bottom 25%. LLM text generation with a small 135M model performs at an average rate of 102.6 tokens/sec, but drops to a poor 5.03 tokens/sec for a medium 7B model.

From a resource density perspective, the E8s_v3 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for memory-bound workloads that do not require high-frequency CPU performance. The trade-off lies in its modest processing speeds and lower computational throughput, as evidenced by weak results in compression and static web serving. This server is best suited for relational databases, caching layers with moderate write demands, software compilation, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that benefit from Premium Storage capabilities.
